g.text: A container is not a small VM: it shares the host kernel
Isolation comes from kernel features (namespaces + cgroups), not from a second operating system.
Each VM boots a full operating system.
Heavy: GBs of RAM, boots in seconds-minutes.
Containers are ordinary processes with a restricted view.
Light: MBs of RAM, start in milliseconds.
Docker Desktop on Windows/macOS runs a small Linux VM so that Linux containers have a Linux kernel to share. (Windows also has its own separate "Windows
